provisional_rulings.question: Q09 — 130 answer labels carry no grammatical gender.
provisional_rulings.ruling: Gender assigned by two productive rules: Welsh verb-nouns are masculine, and unadapted loanwords default to masculine. 56 labels take g, one takes b (saethyddiaeth, -aeth), one is unresolved (marchogaeth), and 10 need no gender because they never head a noun phrase. Confidence is recorded per row on sheet 23.
provisional_rulings.alternative: Leave gender blank and block FT-20, FT-33 and every answer-headed superlative.
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist; confirmed by the translator 2026-09-21 (handover sheet 4 rule 35: Correct)

provisional_rulings.question: ZERO-003 — a nil count with a negative predicate stacks two negatives.
provisional_rulings.ruling: ANSWER-SELECTION RECAST: state what was not chosen rather than what was not said — “Ni ddewisodd yr un o’r chwe disgybl ‘Dim yn aml’ na ‘Byth’.” Faithful to the English, no stacked negation, and it matches how the data was actually collected.
provisional_rulings.alternative: FT-11’s positive-inverse branch (“Dywedodd pob un … fod …”), which is cleaner Welsh but infers the complement of a closed scale rather than translating what the English says.
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist; confirmed by the translator 2026-09-21 (handover sheet 4 rule 10: Correct)

provisional_rulings.question: D48 — no neutral third-person singular exists for a pupil whose sex the view does not carry.
provisional_rulings.ruling: IMPERSONAL RECAST: avoid the pronoun entirely (“Nodwyd gan un disgybl …”) rather than defaulting to masculine.
provisional_rulings.alternative: Masculine as the unmarked default, which is traditional but assigns a sex to a real child the survey did not record.
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist + Sport Wales; confirmed by the translator 2026-09-21 (handover sheet 4 rule 11: Correct)

provisional_rulings.question: Q12 — a or ac before the negative particles ni / nid.
provisional_rulings.ruling: AC. “ac ni chymerodd”, “ac nid oedd”. ni/nid is treated as a consonant-initial function word of the class that takes ac.
provisional_rulings.alternative: Keep a, or recast the sentence so the coordination does not arise.
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist; confirmed by the translator 2026-09-21 (handover sheet 4 rule 21: Correct)

provisional_rulings.question: Q04 — whether unadapted sport names mutate.
provisional_rulings.ruling: THEY DO NOT MUTATE. BMX, Boccia, Parkour, Taekwondo and the other unadapted loans are exempt, consistent with the existing exceptions register.
provisional_rulings.alternative: Mutate them by their initial letter like any other noun.
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist; confirmed by the translator 2026-09-21 (handover sheet 4 rule 27: Correct)

provisional_rulings.question: Q19 — agreement after the coordinated ‘camp neu weithgaredd’.

provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist; confirmed by the translator 2026-09-21 (handover sheet 4 rule 36: Correct)

provisional_rulings.question: Q25 — possessive, pronoun and preposition agreement for a singleton whose sex the view does not carry.
provisional_rulings.ruling: AGREE WITH THE GRAMMATICAL GENDER OF THE ANTECEDENT NOUN: yr unig ddisgybl (m) → ei ysgol, ei ethnigrwydd, ganddo; yr unig ferch → ei hysgol, ei hethnigrwydd, ganddi; yr unig fachgen → as disgybl. This is noun agreement, not an assumption about the pupil, and it is how Welsh treats "y disgybl … ei waith" in every register.
provisional_rulings.alternative: PR-03 impersonal recast of the whole clause (avoids the possessive but lengthens every N=1 qualifier), or "ganddo neu ganddi".
provisional_rulings.volume: 45 unknown-sex singleton clauses in V4.5; every N=1 view in any school
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist; confirmed by the translator 2026-09-21 (handover sheet 4 rule 11: Correct)

provisional_rulings.question: Q26 — the locked English f2 omits the cohort qualifier that the Welsh realises.

provisional_rulings.alternative: Drop the qualifier from the Welsh to match the English, which makes the Welsh sentence less true.
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Report owner

provisional_rulings.question: D61 — f6 parenthetical "(apart from the answer defining this selected group)" is not realised in Welsh.
provisional_rulings.ruling: REALISE IT: "(ac eithrio’r ateb sy’n diffinio’r grŵp hwn)". The parenthetical is a role on the fact record (exclusion of the defining answer) and both languages consume it.
provisional_rulings.alternative: Suppress it in both languages by a shared presentation flag, which changes the locked English.
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist (wording); report owner (flag)

provisional_rulings.question: D71 — the stacked-chart caption must state the rendered count; Welsh wording of the count-aware frame.
provisional_rulings.ruling: "{k:count camp, definite} a ddewiswyd amlaf yn y golwg hwn — {desc}": Y deg camp …, Y naw camp …, Yr wyth camp …, Y chwe champ …, Y pum camp …, Y pedair camp …, Y tair camp …, Y ddwy gamp …; at one, "Y gamp a ddewiswyd amlaf yn y golwg hwn — {desc}". camp is feminine: after the article only dwy lenites (y ddwy gamp — D26: y pedair camp, y pum camp stay unmutated), chwe takes the aspirate (chwe champ), 3/4 take the feminine tair/pedair — all realised by the numeral service (NUM_count_np definite, after_article), never typed.
provisional_rulings.alternative: A numberless frame: "Y campau a ddewiswyd amlaf yn y golwg hwn — {desc}" (avoids the count entirely).
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist (wording); software (the fact)

provisional_rulings.question: Q16 / D76 — the no-report marker in tables and bars.
provisional_rulings.ruling: LANGUAGE-NEUTRAL "—" in the cell or bar in BOTH languages, with aria-label / title from ui.table_suppressed ("Wedi’i atal" / "Suppressed"). No Welsh abbreviation is invented; no English abbreviation is shown in Welsh mode.
provisional_rulings.alternative: A Welsh abbreviation (none is established); or keep "n/r" in English mode as a catalogue exception (D73).
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist + report owner

provisional_rulings.question: FT-11 / Q24 — a nil-count sentence whose defining cohort is itself negative ("Ni ddywedodd yr un o’r 13 disgybl … a ddywedodd nad ydynt … fod …").
provisional_rulings.ruling: RETAIN THE FAITHFUL CLAUSE-BOUNDED CONSTRUCTION UNCHANGED until the linguist rules, and LOCK THE RECORD SET: the 571 strict records (576 occurrences; 1,013 in the wider review class) are enumerated in the baseline and the gate fails if the set changes without a ruling. The ruling, when given, is recorded here as a data value (retain / affirmative_zero / noun_phrase / other) with its branch conditions and four approved fixtures, and applied by regeneration under D82.
provisional_rulings.alternative: Recast now to an affirmative-zero or noun-phrase construction before the ruling (invents a form the linguist has not approved).
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Welsh linguist (wording); report owner (application)

provisional_rulings.question: Sheet 23 — twelve sport labels the live survey offers (S16) that the prototype school's export did not contain: their gender, initial class and mutability.
provisional_rulings.ruling: FEATURES BY THE CONFIRMED RULES: verb-noun heads and unadapted loans masculine (PR-01), unadapted loans exempt from mutation (PR-05 / EX-04), pêl- compounds feminine and plural nouns ‘plural’ as the sheet's sibling rows; Street Dance's sibling Morris Dancing takes Street Dance's own features. The Welsh strings themselves are S16's, verbatim.
provisional_rulings.alternative: Leave the rows out and fail any school build in which a pupil reported one of the twelve sports (D44 fail-loud); or assign features by guesswork.
provisional_rulings.volume: 12 labels; 1,868 pupil mentions Wales-wide in the cleansed dataset
provisional_rulings.ruled_by: Industryline, by the translator-confirmed rules; the translator signs sheet 23

handoff.en: Welcome to your school’s results
handoff.cy: Croeso i ganlyniadau eich ysgol

handoff.en: The School Sport Survey is one of the largest per-capita opportunities in the world for children and young people to have their say on sport. The survey would not be possible without the time and commitment of schools, teachers and pupils like you. Thank you for helping us build a clearer picture of how children and young people experience sport in Wales, and how they want sport to look in the future.
handoff.cy: Yr Arolwg Chwaraeon Ysgol yw un o’r cyfleoedd y pen mwyaf yn y byd i blant a phobl ifanc gael dweud eu dweud am chwaraeon. Ni fyddai’r arolwg yn bosibl heb amser ac ymrwymiad ysgolion, athrawon a disgyblion fel chi. Diolch am ein helpu i lunio darlun cliriach o brofiad plant a phobl ifanc o chwaraeon yng Nghymru, a sut hoffent i chwaraeon edrych yn y dyfodol.

handoff.en: Within each section, you’ll find questions that aim to help consider the findings and what they might mean for your school. We hope it helps you celebrate what’s working well, identify opportunities for development, and support conversations about how to create even more positive sporting experiences for all learners.
handoff.cy: O fewn pob adran, cewch gwestiynau sy’n anelu at helpu i ystyried y canfyddiadau a beth y gallent ei olygu i’ch ysgol chi. handoff.en: Together, your responses are helping Sport Wales, schools and partners across Wales better understand what matters most to children and young people, ensuring that future decisions are informed by their voices.

handoff.en: Percentages represent the share of the base. handoff.en: There are two reasons why percentages may not add to 100%. Firstly, figures are rounded to the nearest whole percent, and so overall figures may not add exactly to 100%. Yn ail, lle gallai disgyblion roi tic i fwy nag un ateb, mae canrannau’n disgrifio cyfran y disgyblion a ddewisodd yr opsiwn hwnnw, yn hytrach na segmentau o’r cyfan.

handoff.en: Some questions were only asked of certain pupils (for example, follow-up questions about a setting are asked only of pupils who used that setting), some pupils left questions blank, and multi-choice questions count every selection — so totals can be smaller or larger than the number of pupil responses. handoff.cy: Dim ond i rai disgyblion pennodol y gofynnwyd rhai cwestiynau (er enghraifft, gofynnwyd gwestynnau dilynol am leoliad penodol dim ond I’r disgyblion a ddefnyddiwyd y lleoliad yno), gadawodd rhai disgyblion gwestiynau’n wag, ac mae cwestiynau amlddewis yn cyfrif pob dewis – felly, gall cyfansymiau fod yn llai neu’n fwy na chyfanswm nifer y disgyblion. handoff.en: Responses become hidden when there is a risk of being able to identify an individual pupil via the information presented. In turn, information is suppressed to protect pupil identity, in line with GDPR. This often happens when too many filters are applied, and pupil numbers fall low enough to potentially identify the pupil who gave those responses.

handoff.en: The vision for sport in Wales is an active nation, where as many people as possible are inspired to be active through sport. This chapter explores how often pupils are active through sport, in which settings pupils do sport, and how participation levels change between different settings. handoff.en: Pupils were asked to complete the sentence “I would do more sport if...” by selecting the best answer from the list of options below. Pupils could choose more than one option. Pupils could also type in their answer if none of the options suited them.
handoff.cy: Gofynnwyd i ddisgyblion gwblhau’r frawddeg “Byddwn i’n gwneud mwy o chwaraeon os...” trwy ddewis yr ateb gorau o blith y rhestr opsiynau isod. Gallai disgyblion ddewis mwy nag un opsiwn. Gallai disgyblion deipio eu hateb hefyd os nad oedd yr un o’r opsiynau yn addas iddynt.

handoff.en: Enjoyment across settings

handoff.en: Pupils reported how much they enjoy sport in PE lessons, school sports clubs, clubs outside school, and other settings like the park or garden. Reportable answers on each of the four charts can be selected to filter the wider report by the pupils who gave that answer.

Gall atebion adroddadwy ar bob un o’r pedair siart gael eu dewis i hidlo’r adroddiad ehangach yn ôl y disgyblion a roddodd yr ateb hwnnw.

handoff.en: How does enjoyment differ between groups of pupils?

handoff.en: Enjoyment can differ between groups and change as pupils get older. The table shows how many pupils in each year group said they enjoy sport ‘a lot’ in each setting.

handoff.en: Do our pupils feel listened to?

handoff.en: How confident do our pupils feel?
handoff.cy: Pa mor hyderus y mae ein disgyblion yn teimlo?

handoff.en: Pupils were asked how confident they are in and around sport in four different ways; trying a new sport, learning a new skill, trying again when sport is hard, and trying sport in a new place.
handoff.cy: Gofynnwyd i ddisgyblion pa mor hyderus ydynt o ran chwaraeon mewn pedair ffordd wahanol: rhoi cynnig ar gamp newydd, dysgu sgil newydd, rhoi cynnig arall arni pan fydd camp yn anodd, a rhoi cynnig ar gamp mewn lle newydd.

handoff.en: What are Free School Meal Quartiles?

handoff.en: Sport Wales uses the proportion of pupils eligible for Free School Meals (FSM) as an indicator of deprivation. Schools are grouped into four FSM quartiles based on the proportion of pupils eligible for Free School Meals.
handoff.cy: Mae Chwaraeon Cymru yn defnyddio cyfran y disgyblion sy’n gymwys i gael Prydau Ysgol am Ddim (PYDd) fel dangosydd amddifadedd. Caiff ysgolion eu grwpio’n bedwar chwartel PYDd ar sail cyfran y disgyblion sy’n gymwys i gael Prydau Ysgol am Ddim.

handoff.en: Note: These quartiles provide a high-level measure of deprivation at school level. They do not indicate the individual circumstances of pupils attending those schools. Pupils experiencing deprivation may attend schools in any FSM quartile.
handoff.cy: Sylwch: Mae’r chwarteli hyn yn cynnig mesur lefel uchel o amddifadedd ar lefel ysgol. Nid ydynt yn dangos amgylchiadau unigol y disgyblion sy’n mynd i’r ysgolion hynny. Gall disgyblion sy’n profi amddifadedd fynd i ysgolion mewn unrhyw chwartel PYDd.

handoff.en: A light grey bar cannot be selected as a filter. This includes response options that did not meet the whole-school eligibility threshold of five for use as a filter. Counts below five may still be displayed within an otherwise reportable demographic view. A dark grey bar marked “—” is suppressed: the value is not reportable in the current view.
handoff.cy: Nid yw bar llwyd golau’n gallu cael ei ddewis fel hidlydd. Mae hyn yn cynnwys opsiynau ymateb na wnaethant gyrraedd y trothwy cymhwysedd ysgol gyfan i’w ddefnyddio fel hidlydd, sef pump. Gall niferoedd o dan 5 gael eu harddangos o hyd o fewn gwedd ddemograffig y gellir adrodd arni fel arall. Mae bar llwyd tywyll gyda “—” ynddo yn guddiedig: ni ellir adrodd y gwerth hwn yn y wedd bresennol.

handoff.en: Results are unweighted counts of pupil responses — real answers from real pupils, with nothing scaled up. Every sentence names the group it describes. A worked example: “Boxing and football were tied as the most frequently selected sports, with seven selections each, among Year 5 boys” — “tied” means both were selected by the same number of pupils, and “among Year 5 boys” tells you the finding applies only to that group.
handoff.cy: Mae’r canlyniadau yn niferoedd heb eu pwysoli o ymatebion disgyblion, sef atebion real gan ddisgyblion real, heb gynyddu dim yn gymesur. Mae pob brawddeg yn enwi’r grŵp y mae’n ei ddisgrifio. Dyma enghraifft ymarferol: “Y campau a ddewiswyd amlaf oedd bocsio a phêl-droed yn gyfartal, gyda saith dewis yr un, ymhlith bechgyn Blwyddyn 5” — ystyr “yn gyfartal” yw bod y ddwy gamp wedi’u dewis gan yr un nifer o ddisgyblion, ac mae “ymhlith bechgyn Blwyddyn 5” yn dweud wrthych mai dim ond i’r grŵp hwnnw y mae’r canfyddiad yn berthnasol.

handoff.en: Dark grey bars represent suppressed data — values that cannot be shown because the group behind them is too small to report safely. Light grey bars are options that cannot be selected as filters, as the data can become misleading when not considered in the context of the way the question was asked. Whole sections may also appear greyed out with a message when the group you have selected is too small to provide insights. If you continue scrolling, there may still be insights and information in other sections that have not been suppressed, depending on the amount of data available.
handoff.cy: Mae barrau llwyd tywyll yn cynrychioli data cuddiedig – gwerthoedd na ellir eu dangos gan fod y grŵp wrth wraidd y data yn rhy fach i adrodd arno’n ddiogel. Mae barrau llwyd golau yn opsiynau na allant gael eu dewis fel hidlyddion oherwydd gall y data gamarwain pan na fydd yn cael ei ystyried yng nghyd-destun y ffordd y gofynnwyd y cwestiwn. Hefyd, gall adrannau cyfan ymddangos mewn llwyd gyda neges pan fyddwch wedi dewis grŵp sy’n rhy fach i gynnig mewnwelediadau. Os byddwch yn parhau i sgrolio, gall fod mewnwelediadau a gwybodaeth mewn adrannau eraill sydd heb gael eu cuddio, yn dibynnu ar faint o ddata sydd ar gael.

handoff.en: FSM Q4 includes schools with the highest proportion of pupils eligible for FSM. This quartile represents the 25% of schools with the highest levels of deprivation in Wales.
handoff.cy: Mae Ch4 PYDd yn cynnwys ysgolion sydd â’r gyfran uchaf o ddisgyblion sy’n gymwys i gael PYDd. Mae’r chwartel hwn yn cynrychioli’r 25% o ysgolion sydd â’r lefelau uchaf o amddifadedd yng Nghymru.

handoff.en: Latent demand is where pupils say they would like to do more of a particular sport. More than one sport could be selected.

handoff.en: Unmet demand refers to sports that pupils said they would like to do more of, but have not participated in since the start of the academic year. This may highlight where pupils have demand that is not currently being met. Please note, the 2026 survey newly captures information on sports pupils did in PE or Lesson time. In turn, Unmet Demand is calculated differently in 2026 compared with 2022, as it accounts for sports done in PE or Lesson Time, whilst previous Unmet Demand calculations could not. Caution is therefore advised if comparing with previous survey findings.
handoff.cy: Mae galw heb ei fodloni yn cyfeirio at chwaraeon y dywedodd disgyblion yr hoffent wneud mwy ohonynt, ond nad ydynt wedi cymryd rhan ynddynt ers dechrau’r flwyddyn academaidd. Gallai hyn amlygu ble mae gan ddisgyblion alw nad yw’n cael ei fodloni ar hyn o bryd. Sylwch, mae arolwg 2026 yn cipio o’r newydd wybodaeth am chwaraeon a wnaed gan ddisgyblion mewn AG neu amser gwersi. Yn ei dro, mae Galw heb ei fodloni yn cael ei gyfrifo’n wahanol yn 2026 o gymharu â 2022, gan ei fod yn cyfrif am chwaraeon a wnaed mewn AG neu amser gwersi. Ni allai cyfrifiadau blaenorol o Alw heb ei fodloni wneud hyn. Felly, dylid cymryd gofal wrth gymharu â chanfyddiadau’r arolwg blaenorol.
